description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/latlon3d/rules/ppm_D_lev_mono_noflux_bc (MONOTONE conservative flux-form vertical PPM: full Colella-Woodward 1984 -- eq (1.6) edge on eq (1.8) monotonized slopes plus the eq (1.10) parabola limiter -- no-flux top/surface) driven by problems/latlon3d_advection_vertical_ppm_mono.esm, with passive lon (NLON=8) and lat (NLAT=5). Loaded once per resolution binding NLEV; pe / dz / w_edge re-derive from NLEV each rebinding. Forced-steady u*=cos(pi z) transported by w=sin(pi z) (vanishing at both walls -> exact no-flux mass conservation, unaffected by limiting); the t=0.1 drift is the flux-divergence truncation on the quadratic-stretch mesh. HONEST ORDER: this is the LIMITED chain, so the order is deliberately sub-nominal. The Julia golden gives median observed order ~2.44 in L2 and ~1.92 in Linf on the NLEV = 8/16/32/64 ladder (~2.48/~1.97 asymptotically, on a finer ladder), versus the clean 4.0/3.9 of the identical-in-every-other-respect UNLIMITED sibling sweep latlon3d_advection_vertical_ppm -- the two goldens differ ONLY by the imported rule, so their ratio IS the measured cost of monotonicity. The cause is the classic CW84 smooth-extremum clip: cos(pi z) has its extrema exactly AT the two walls (cos'(0)=cos'(pi)=0), which is where eqs (1.8)/(1.10) clip hardest, so the error concentrates in a few boundary cells and Linf lags L2. expected_order 2.2 with order_tolerance 0.4 brackets BOTH norm medians honestly (deviation ~0.24 in L2, ~0.28 in Linf); this is NOT a claim of 3rd-order convergence, which the CW84 limiter forecloses on any smooth profile whose extrema trigger the clip (the extremum-preserving Colella-Sekora (2008) limiter is the documented follow-on that would recover it). This smooth-MMS sweep measures ORDER only; the property the monotone rule EXISTS for -- boundedness on sharp gradients, where the unlimited sibling drives a tracer negative -- is a structural claim carried by the rule, not by this sweep. expected_order and order_tolerance are set from the Julia golden. RESOLUTION LADDER (why 8/16/32/64, not the unlimited sibling's 16/32/64/128): the eq (1.10) parabola limiter must inline BOTH of the upwind cell's reconstructed edges about five times each, and a let-free expression AST cannot share them, so the lowered monotone body is ~25x the unlimited body (13.9 MB vs 0.55 MB of expanded AST at NLEV=6) and the RHS is ~25x costlier to evaluate. The coarser ladder measures the same order (L2 2.44 / Linf 1.92 here vs 2.48 / 1.97 at 16-128, pairwise orders converging monotonically) at about a quarter of the cost, keeping the sweep tractable in CI. This AST blow-up is a property of the let-free AST, not of the scheme; a common-subexpression / let construct in ESM (or a formulation that materializes the cell-edge reconstruction as its own array) would remove it, and is the documented follow-on.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
